verses.zh: （以东人多益来告诉扫罗说：大卫到了亚希米勒家。那时，大卫作这训诲诗，交与伶长。）勇士啊，你为何以作恶自夸？　神的慈爱是常存的。
verses.en: For the music director, a well-written song[NOTE:1] by David. It was written when Doeg the Edomite went and informed Saul: “David has arrived at the home of Ahimelech.”[NOTE:2] Why do you boast about your evil plans,[NOTE:3] O powerful man?God’s loyal love protects me all day long.[NOTE:4]
notes: Psalm 52. The psalmist confidently confronts his enemy and affirms that God will destroy evildoers and vindicate the godly.

The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. The word is derived from a verb meaning “to be prudent; to be wise.” Various options are: “a contemplative song,” “a song imparting moral wisdom,” or “a skillful [i.e., well-written] song.” The term occurs in the superscriptions of Pss 32, 42, 44, 45, 52-55, 74, 78, 88, 89, and 142, as well as in Ps 47:7.

According to the superscription, David wrote this psalm during the period when Saul was seeking his life. On one occasion Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s head shepherd (1 Sam 21:7), informed Saul of David’s whereabouts (see 1 Sam 21-22).tn Heb “when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul and said to him, ‘David has come to the house of Ahimelech.’”
Heb “Why do you boast in evil?”

verses.zh: 你的舌头邪恶诡诈，好像剃头刀，快利伤人。
verses.en: Your tongue carries out your destructive plans;[NOTE:1] it is as effective as a sharp razor, O deceiver.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the loyal love of God [is] all the day.” In this context, where the psalmist is threatened by his enemy, the point seems to be that the psalmist is protected by God’s loyal love at all times.
Heb “destruction your tongue devises.”

verses.zh: 你爱恶胜似爱善，又爱说谎，不爱说公义。（细拉）
verses.en: You love evil more than good,lies more than speaking the truth.[NOTE:1] (Selah)
notes: Heb “like a sharpened razor, doer of deceit.” The masculine participle עָשָׂה (ʿasah) is understood as a substantival vocative, addressed to the powerful man.

verses.zh: 诡诈的舌头啊，你爱说一切毁灭的话！
verses.en: You love to use all the words that destroy,[NOTE:1] and the tongue that deceives.
notes: Or “deceit more than speaking what is right.”

verses.zh: 神也要毁灭你，直到永远；他要把你拿去，从你的帐棚中抽出，从活人之地将你拔出。（细拉）
verses.en: Yet[NOTE:1] God will make you a permanent heap of ruins.[NOTE:2] He will scoop you up[NOTE:3] and remove you from your home;[NOTE:4] he will uproot you from the land of the living. (Selah)
notes: Heb “you love all the words of swallowing.” Traditionally בַּלַּע (balaʿ) has been taken to mean “swallowing” in the sense of “devouring” or “destructive” (see BDB 118 s.v. בָּלַע). HALOT 135 s.v. III *בֶּלַע proposes a homonym here, meaning “confusion.” This would fit the immediate context nicely and provide a close parallel to the following line, which refers to deceptive words.
The adverb גַּם (gam, “also; even”) is translated here in an adversative sense (“yet”). It highlights the contrastive correspondence between the evildoer’s behavior and God’s response.
Heb “will tear you down forever.”
This rare verb (חָתָה, khatah) occurs only here and in Prov 6:27; 25:22; Isa 30:14.

verses.zh: 义人要看见而惧怕，并要笑他，
verses.en: When the godly see this, they will be filled with awe,and will mock the evildoer, saying:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from [your] tent.”

verses.zh: 说：看哪，这就是那不以　神为他力量的人，只倚仗他丰富的财物，在邪恶上坚立自己。
verses.en: “Look, here is the man who would not make[NOTE:1] God his protector.He trusted in his great wealthand was confident about his plans to destroy others.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the godly will see and will fear and at him will laugh.”

The imperfect verbal form here draws attention to the ongoing nature of the action. The evildoer customarily rejected God and trusted in his own abilities. Another option is to take the imperfect as generalizing, “[here is the man who] does not make.”

verses.zh: 至于我，就像　神殿中的青橄榄树；我永永远远倚靠　神的慈爱。
verses.en: But I[NOTE:1] am like a flourishing[NOTE:2] olive tree in the house of God;I continually[NOTE:3] trust in God’s loyal love.
notes: Heb “he was strong in his destruction.” “Destruction” must refer back to the destructive plans mentioned in v. 2. The verb (derived from the root עָזַז, ʿazaz, “be strong”) as it stands is either an imperfect (if so, probably used in a customary sense) or a preterite (without vav [ו] consecutive). However the form should probably be emended to וַיָּעָז (vayyaʿaz), a Qal preterite (with vav [ו] consecutive) from עָזַז. Note the preterite form without vav (ו) consecutive in the preceding line (וַיִּבְטַח, vayyivtakh, “and he trusted”). The prefixed vav (ו) was likely omitted by haplography (note the suffixed vav [ו] on the preceding עָשְׁרוֹ, ʿoshro, “his wealth”).
The disjunctive construction (vav [ו] + subject) highlights the contrast between the evildoer’s destiny (vv. 5-7) and that of the godly psalmist’s security.
Or “luxuriant, green, leafy.”

verses.zh: 我要称谢你，直到永远，因为你行了这事。我也要在你圣民面前仰望你的名；这名本为美好。
verses.en: I will continually[NOTE:1] thank you when[NOTE:2] you execute judgment;[NOTE:3] I will rely on[NOTE:4] you,[NOTE:5] for your loyal followers know you are good.[NOTE:6]
notes: Or, hyperbolically, “forever and ever.”
Or, hyperbolically, “forever.”
Or “for.”

Heb “you have acted.” The perfect verbal form (1) probably indicates a future perfect here. The psalmist promises to give thanks when the expected vindication has been accomplished. Other options include (2) a generalizing (“for you act”) or (3) rhetorical (“for you will act”) use.
Or “wait on.”
Heb “your name.” God’s “name” refers here to his reputation and revealed character.
